fichas.title: Scientific Libraries
fichas.summary: Scientific libraries support education and research by collecting printed publications and other information media and making them available for use. They provide reading rooms, lending from closed stacks and self-service shelves, and access to teaching materials and special collections. Services may include remote lending, copying, and enlargement of microforms. Reading-place provision relates to student numbers, while subject classification supports orientation.
uses: Storing and consulting books and other information media

fichas.title: University Libraries
fichas.summary: University libraries may be single- or two-storey buildings. Single-storey systems are centrally administered and may include user areas in branch or specialist libraries. Two-storey systems combine a central library with libraries serving faculties, specialist areas, and institutes. Stock may be freely available in reading rooms, self-service stacks, or closed stacks; the mix depends on the collection, organisational concept, and available space.

fichas.title: Juridicum Halle Specialist Law Library
fichas.summary: Example of a specialist law library at Halle University, Wittenberg. The illustrated project includes reading rooms on multiple floors, a ground-floor entrance area, and a section. The plan key identifies visitor, staff, study, service, and support spaces. Architects: Thomas van den Valentyn and Gernot Schulz.
